No allegation is treated as proof of conditionality.","closed_system_silence":"Low nationally in this open, heavily audited system, but incomplete subnational reporting and decentralized delivery can conceal local misconduct, exclusion, or implementation failure.","duplicate_reporting":"Material overlap exists among official releases and their administrative datasets, including Census/CPS reporting, Treasury-era corroboration, VA uptake releases, and repeated use of the same #WeCount report. These should not be treated as independent corroboration; the ledger's WEB-to-WD ID reconciliation and overlapping #WeCount entries require deterministic deduplication.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Yes. The notebook presents favorable policy/enactment and delivery evidence alongside poverty, food insecurity, affordability, learning-loss, equity, housing, disability-access, water-oversight, and post-Dobbs contrary evidence.","missing_source_type":"Independent beneficiary-level and state/local implementation evaluations are missing for completed water projects, PACT benefits and health outcomes, ESSER learning recovery, childcare continuity, and post-Dobbs access. For 6B.7, a completed watchdog investigation, substantiated complaint, enforcement record, or allocation analysis capable of testing partisan conditionality is missing.","official_claim_independence":"Partially addressed by GAO, inspectors general, courts, Census/CDC/USDA measurement, KFF, Commonwealth Fund, Preventive Medicine, and #WeCount. However, CMS enrollment, EPA allocation, VA uptake, and ACF reach claims remain primarily official administrative claims and do not independently establish effective access or outcomes.","open_system_complaint_volume":"High visibility and adversarial oversight can amplify isolated allegations or litigation; WEB-6B-C2-005 is correctly kept as an allegation only. Conversely, public complaint volume is not a prevalence measure.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Addressed well: the notebook distinguishes presidential, congressional, agency, state/local, provider, and household roles; flags the exceptional 2021 relief baseline; and identifies COVID, inflation, Ukraine-related price shocks, Dobbs, judicial constraints, and federalism. Residual uncertainty remains for heterogeneous local exposure and beneficiary outcomes.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WD001","WD005","WD006","WD007","WD008","WD011","WD013","WEB-6B-C1-002","WEB-6B-C1-007","WEB-6B-C2-001","WEB-6B-C2-004","WEB-6B-C2-005"],"unresolved_risks":["Published 2022 supplemental-poverty estimates are explicitly provisional pending Census revision after the disclosed threshold-coding error.","Several favorable records establish enactment, allocations, plans, claims, screenings, selections, or spending—not completed benefits, quality, or causal beneficiary outcomes.","Political-conditionality evidence is a bounded credible null, not proof of absence; subnational conduct remains insufficiently observable.","Some later audits illuminate 2022 systems or partial periods but cannot establish that identified weaknesses were caused or corrected in 2022.","The dossier contains many official and audit sources but fewer independent beneficiary-level evaluations across decentralized welfare delivery."]},"chapter_id":"6B","defensible_evidence_estimate":32,"independent_source_family_estimate":20,"missing_themes":["Completed 2022 water-project, lead-exposure, sanitation, and beneficiary-outcome evidence.","Independent 2022 PACT adjudication, health-care access, and health-outcome evidence.","Calendar-2022 causal evaluation of ESSER learning recovery and durable local capacity.","Subnational welfare-administration and political-conditionality findings, including substantiated complaints or enforcement outcomes.","Disability and HCBS access beyond non-comparable waiting-list measures.","Long-run housing supply, childcare continuity, and post-Dobbs maternal/reproductive access outcomes."],"substantive_issues":["The same original evidence is represented under initial WEB IDs and later WD ledger IDs; retain one canonical stable record per source-locator-claim fact with many-to-many lens mappings.","WEB-6B-C1-009 and WEB-6B-C2-001 derive from the same #WeCount report and should not count as independent corroboration; retain distinct claims only if separately needed.","Some source records combine multiple closely related numerical and interpretive propositions; judges should rely on the documented locator and retain the stated period and attribution limits.","WEB-6B-C1-004 and WEB-6B-C1-005 establish oversight-system weaknesses relevant to 2022 but explicitly include pre-BIL performance; they cannot be read as first-year BIL causal findings."]}],"global_findings":["Terminal conclusion: permitted research rounds were exhausted without full saturation; this is not a claim that the dossier is complete.","The selected 6B scope has broad, mixed, target-period evidence with explicit authority, baseline, and shock qualifications, but outcome and attribution certainty is uneven across decentralized programs.","Residual gaps remain material for downstream confidence and interpretation, especially beneficiary outcomes, local implementation, causal effects, and political conditionality. Missing evidence is not adverse evidence."],"needs_continuation":false,"reviewer_summary":"Terminal no-search evidence-quality review for 6B only. The dossier is usable as a mixed evidence handoff if official implementation claims, later audits, repeated-source overlap, and attribution limits are preserved; it does not establish complete welfare delivery or a conclusive null on political conditionality.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":[]}
